text_copy_copy_copy_.text:
The majority of vertebral compression fractures go undiagnosed1

Early recognition and intervention can help patients avoid fracture progression, prolonged pain, loss of mobility and additional complications associated with untreated vertebral compression fractures (VCFs).2,3

standaloneimage.alt: Left untreated, patients can face long-term complications known as the “downward spiral”

text_copy_copy_copy_.text:
Why early diagnosis matters

VCFs, caused by thinning bones, tumors or other complications, are associated with significant morbidity and mortality.11


It is estimated that approximately 50% of women and 25% of men will experience an osteoporotic fracture during their lifetime.12

text_copy_copy_copy_.text:
How Janet recovered from a vertebral compression fracture

After experiencing persistent lower back pain following a fall, Janet consulted her physician and was diagnosed with a T11 vertebral compression fracture (VCF).

Janet worked with Dr. Jason Smith to review her treatment options before undergoing kyphoplasty, a minimally invasive procedure to help restore function to her spine. “She did great. She was able to move and came in on her own at two weeks without any sort of independent devices, like a brace or walker. She was back to doing her normal things pretty quickly,” says Dr. Smith.
